prompt.brief: Design an enterprise RAG platform that ingests permissioned documents, retrieves fresh evidence, maintains conversation context, and generates cited answers with safe model fallbacks.
successSignals: Separate source documents, chunk and embedding versions, access-control metadata, conversations, prompts, and model outputs.
Use hybrid dense and sparse retrieval with reranking, bounded context, citations, and tenant-aware filters.
Make indexing asynchronous and versioned so deletes and permission changes cannot leak stale evidence.
Explain prompt injection, hallucination, model failure, feedback evaluation, cost budgets, and auditability.

functional: Upload and parse enterprise documents, chunk and embed them, and publish a searchable version with freshness status.
Answer a question with authorized retrieved passages, citations, conversation context, safety checks, and streamed output.
Support document deletion, permission changes, reindexing, feedback, evaluation sets, usage controls, and tenant export.
nonFunctional: Target p95 time to first token below 500 ms and completed grounded responses below 3 seconds for normal queries.
Scale document indexing and query traffic independently, with per-tenant quotas and bounded retrieval work.
Never lose a source document or feedback event; make embedding, indexing, generation, and tool retries safe.
Fall back to keyword search, a smaller model, or an explicit no-answer response when dependencies fail.
scaleAssumptions: Support 10,000 queries per second, 100 million indexed chunks, and thousands of enterprise tenants.
Partition by tenant and knowledge collection; isolate large reindex jobs and hot assistants.
Retain encrypted source and audit data while keeping vector indexes, conversation context, and caches bounded.

dataFlow.title: Accept Ingest and index enterprise documents
dataFlow.description: The Enterprise RAG platform gateway authenticates the caller, validates the request, applies tenant policy and idempotency, then routes it to the owning service.

dataFlow.title: Commit the durable state
dataFlow.description: The platform records a versioned document ingestion request and conversation turn before indexing or generation.

dataFlow.title: Publish the domain event
dataFlow.description: A durable outbox publishes committed Enterprise RAG platform events; consumers deduplicate by event ID and track offsets.

dataFlow.title: Build the read model
dataFlow.description: Indexing workers parse versioned documents, preserve ACL metadata, create chunks and embeddings, update lexical/vector indexes, and expose indexing watermarks.

dataFlow.title: Serve and recover asynchronously
dataFlow.description: Serving reads use the Enterprise RAG platform projection; replay, repair, export, and slow work remain off the request path.

architecture.title: Design a conversational AI platform that uses Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) to answer questions from enterprise knowledge bases, maintains conversation context, and provides cited responses. reference architecture
architecture.summary: The ingestion path durably versions documents and asynchronously builds ACL-aware lexical and vector indexes. The query path synchronously enforces authorization, retrieves and reranks evidence, constructs a bounded context, applies safety policy, and routes generation through a model gateway before streaming cited output.

deepDives.title: Consistency and idempotency
points: Keep the Enterprise RAG platform commit authoritative; let derived projections converge with visible version and freshness.
Use idempotency keys, conditional Enterprise RAG platform writes, event IDs, and versions so retries and replay are safe.
Return Enterprise RAG platform version and observedAt so clients can reason about freshness.

deepDives.title: Partitioning and hot keys
points: Partition Enterprise RAG platform by its primary read and write keys, then isolate hot tenants, users, items, or regions.
Bound Enterprise RAG platform work with backpressure and queue isolation so one hot key cannot dominate the cluster.
Keep a replay or reconciliation path for Enterprise RAG platform projection drift and partial failures.

deepDives.title: Failure and recovery
points: Serve the last acceptable Enterprise RAG platform projection or an explicit degraded response when workers fail.
Retain durable Enterprise RAG platform records for replay and make each downstream effect independently retryable.
Measure Enterprise RAG platform latency, backlog, freshness, error rate, and correctness drift.

tradeoffs.title: Strong consistency versus throughput
tradeoffs.recommendation: Strongly protect the business commit and use versioned eventual projections for high-volume reads.
tradeoffs.caution: Making every derived read synchronous increases coordination and tail latency.

tradeoffs.title: Push versus pull processing
tradeoffs.recommendation: Push bounded events to workers and pull durable snapshots on reads or recovery.
tradeoffs.caution: Unbounded fanout or full scans make bursts and hot keys expensive.

tradeoffs.title: Managed service versus custom control
tradeoffs.recommendation: Start with managed primitives where their limits match the access pattern, then isolate replaceable interfaces.
tradeoffs.caution: Provider defaults do not remove the need for quotas, replay, observability, and data lifecycle design.

commonMistakes: Putting all work on the synchronous request path.
Choosing a data store before writing the access patterns and consistency contract.
Ignoring retries, duplicate events, late data, deletion, privacy, or authorization.
Leaving hot partitions, backpressure, stale reads, and recovery unspecified.
Allowing unbounded requests or exports to compete with normal traffic.

followUps.question: What happens when the primary worker is unavailable?
followUps.answer: Acknowledge only after the durable boundary, serve the last acceptable projection, queue retryable work, and replay or reconcile after recovery.

followUps.question: How would you support a tenfold traffic spike?
followUps.answer: Pre-scale partitions, apply admission control and backpressure, isolate hot keys, cache immutable snapshots, and make freshness degradation visible.

followUps.question: How do you verify correctness?
followUps.answer: Use idempotency metrics, version gaps, sampled source-to-projection comparisons, replay tests, and a shadow rebuild before repair.

rubric.description: The answer defines ingestion, authorized retrieval, cited generation, scale, durability, and failure contracts.
Entities and document/tenant/conversation keys support ACL-safe RAG, citations, privacy, and lifecycle changes.
Partitioning, cache behavior, queues, backpressure, and hot-key handling are explicit.
Idempotency, replay, recovery, degraded reads, and observability protect committed state.
The candidate can explain Enterprise RAG platform consistency, push/pull, managed services, and the scale boundary.
